claims: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
As of April 2026, Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft, as reported by Space.com.
As of April 2026, Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit, as reported by Space.com.
As of April 2026, Artemis III mission does not include immediately landing on the Moon, as reported by Space.com.
As of April 2026, Artemis III mission revision follows concerns over technological readiness, notes SpaceNews and The Guardian.
As of April 2026, Artemis III mission revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
As of April 2026, the actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
As of April 2026, Artemis IV mission is targeted for 2028.
